Question B-001-016-009.

Why the correct answer is right: Fast-scan television on 145 MHz is prohibited because 145 MHz is in the 144 MHz to 148 MHz band with a 30 kHz maximum, and fast-scan ATV occupies more bandwidth than that limit allows.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "FT8 on 14.074 MHz": FT8 is a narrow digital mode, with many FT8 contacts fitting in the space needed for one SSB transmission, so it is not the wide-signal problem here.
- sourceIndex 2: "Morse radiotelegraphy (CW) on 10.145 MHz": CW is the narrowest of the CW/SSB/FM ordering and fits the narrow-band context at 10.145 MHz.
- sourceIndex 3: "Fast-scan television (ATV) on 440 MHz": 440 MHz is outside the 144 MHz to 148 MHz band with the 30 kHz limit, while the bandwidth conflict here is fast-scan ATV at 145 MHz.
